Hearty Steak and Mushroom Pie

Served at: St. Stephen's Day (Boxing Day)

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 2 hours 30 min

On St. Stephen's Day, often known as Boxing Day, families frequently gather for a more relaxed meal after the Christmas feast. This Hearty Steak and Mushroom Pie is a quintessential comfort food, perfect for a chilly winter day, offering rich flavors and satisfying warmth as a delicious centerpiece for holiday enjoyment.

Ingredients

  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) olive oil, divided
  • 2 pounds (900 g) beef chuck, cut into 1-inch (2.5 cm) cubes
  • 1 large (150 g) yellow onion, chopped
  • 2 cloves (10 g) garlic, minced
  • 8 ounces (225 g) cremini mushrooms, quartered
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dark ale or stout
  • 2 cups (480 ml) beef broth
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) dried thyme
  • 1 bay leaf
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 1 sheet (approx. 14 ounces / 400 g) frozen puff pastry, thawed
  • 1 large egg, beaten

Method

  1. Heat 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil in a large Dutch oven or oven-safe pot over medium-high heat.
  2. Season beef cubes generously with salt and pepper, then brown them in batches on all sides, removing to a plate as they are done.
  3. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil to the pot, then add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. Stir in the minced garlic and quartered mushrooms, cooking for another 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender and have released their liquid.
  5. Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute to coat, creating a roux.
  6. Pour in the dark ale, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot, and let it simmer for 2 minutes.
  7. Stir in the beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, dried thyme, and bay leaf, then return the browned beef to the pot.
  8. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1 hour 45 minutes to 2 hours, or until the beef is very tender.
  9. Remove the bay leaf, taste, and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed; let the filling cool completely.
  10. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and lightly grease a 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish.
  11. Pour the cooled beef and mushroom filling into the prepared pie dish.
  12. Unroll the thawed puff pastry and place it over the filling, trimming any excess and crimping the edges to seal.
  13. Cut a few small slits in the top of the pastry to allow steam to escape, then brush the entire surface with the beaten egg.
  14. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and puffed, and the filling is bubbling.
  15. Let the pie rest for 10 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For an even richer flavor, use leftover roast beef from your Christmas dinner instead of fresh chuck, adjusting cooking time for the beef to just heat through and meld with the sauce.
  • Add other root vegetables like diced carrots or parsnips along with the onions for extra heartiness and flavor.
  • This pie can be assembled ahead of time and refrigerated for up to 24 hours before baking; simply add 10-15 minutes to the baking time if baking from cold.
